children: Canada's main stock index ended lower on Friday as technology shares fell, but the index still notched a weekly gain as recent strength in corporate profits offset worries about higher interest rates to tackle inflation.
ended down 31.29 points, or 0.1%, at 36,105.90. For the week, the index gained 0.9%, its second straight weekly advance.
US stocks posted steeper declines on Friday as concerns about Nvidia
pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

"It's a mixed day, ending an up-week. So that theme of resilience continues," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones. "We have corporate profits which continue to exceed expectations ... That is helping to provide a significant offset to a lot of the concerns about AI, technology and inflation."
Economists expect Canada's consumer price index report for October, due on Monday, to show inflation rising to an annual rate of 3.2%.
"If there are any takeaways from this week's US inflation data is that there are some lingering pressures, (and) that policymakers are running out of patience,"  Kourkafas said.
Investors see a 64% chance the Bank of Canada will raise interest rates in December. (0#CADIRPR)

Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) and the materials group, which includes metal mining shares, posted declines of 0.2% and 0.6% respectively. The price of copper (HGc1) was down 2%.
Most other sectors notched gains, including energy, which added 0.9%.
